conventions.convention: Natural units c = ℏ = k_B = 1, signature (−,+,+,+), affine parameter dimension L, Newton constant dimension L², and null-stress variation dimension L⁻⁴.
The reference geometry is stationary precisely when B₀ = 0. Generator labels and affine normalization remain fixed across the dimensionless perturbation parameter.
The adopted focusing law is ∂λδθ = −8πG_NδT_kk with δθ tending to zero at future infinity. Stress variations may have either sign.
The common cut C is nonempty, compact and smooth; the stress has absolutely integrable generator tails and a finite transverse absolute first moment. The background area density is dA₀ = μ₀,λ₀.
“Horizon” means the supplied smooth null hypersurface. The model asserts no event-horizon property, null energy condition, entropy identification or physical accuracy.

The QNEC/QFC source formulations use their own d-dimensional geometry independently of the four-dimensional focusing model. The JT quantum expansion uses positive total dilaton Φ instead of transverse area; rQFC requires its derivative to be nonpositive only where the quantum expansion vanishes.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt, only to first order in ε, ∂λδθ(λ,y) = −8πG_NδT_kk(λ,y), with lim λ→∞ δθ(λ,y) = 0, for the specified differentiable compact-cut stationary-reference family, fixed stress prescription, generator-tail integrability and finite transverse absolute first moment.

Under the stated model and integrability hypotheses, the finite limit δA∞ exists and, for every λ ≥ λ₀, δA∞ − δA(λ) = 8πG_N ∫C dA₀ ∫λ∞ (v−λ)δT_kk(v,y) dv. Consequently (δA∞ − δA(λ))/(4G_N) = 2πMλ. This is a signed geometric identity without an entropy identification.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 calls the transverse stress-tail integral absolutely convergent without spelling out the endpoint argument. At u = λ₀, the first-moment weight vanishes near λ₀, so that bound alone does not directly give the unweighted integral. The stated continuity on compact C × [λ₀,λ₀+1] supplies integrability there; on the remaining tail, v−λ₀ ≥ 1 supplies the bound. Thus the hypotheses suffice, but this short justification is implicit.
